The '''Baik–Deift–Johansson theorem''' is a result from probabilistic [[combinatorics]]. It deals with the [[subsequence]]s of a randomly [[Discrete uniform distribution|uniformly]] drawn [[permutation]] from the set <math>\{1,2,\dots,N\}</math>. The theorem makes a statement about the [[probability distribution|distribution]] of the length of the longest increasing subsequence in the limit. The theorem was influential in [[probability|probability theory]] since it connected the [[Kardar–Parisi–Zhang equation|KPZ-universality]] with the theory of [[random matrix|random matrices]].

The theorem was proven in 1999 by [[Jinho Baik]], [[Percy Deift]] and [[Kurt Johansson (mathematician)|Kurt Johansson]].<ref>{{cite arXiv|first1=Jinho|last1=Baik|first2=Percy|last2=Deift|first3=Kurt|last3=Johansson|title=On the Distribution of the Length of the Longest Increasing Subsequence of Random Permutations |date=1998 |eprint=math/9810105 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | doi=10.1017/CBO9781139872003 | title=The Surprising Mathematics of Longest Increasing Subsequences | year=2015 | last1=Romik | first1=Dan | isbn=9781107075832 }}</ref>

== Statement ==
For each <math>N \geq 1</math> let <math>\pi_N</math> be a uniformly chosen permutation with length <math>N</math>. Let <math>l(\pi_N)</math> be the length of the longest, increasing subsequence of <math>\pi_N</math>.

Then we have for every <math>x \in \mathbb{R}</math> that
:<math>\mathbb{P}\left(\frac{l(\pi_N)-2\sqrt{N}}{N^{1/6}}\leq x \right)\to F_2(x),\quad N \to \infty</math>
where <math>F_2(x)</math> is the [[Tracy-Widom distribution]] of the [[Gaussian unitary ensemble]].
